answer: Plant flawed answers as traps. Each epoch the network slips a few answers with hidden mistakes into grading, such as a sonnet that miscounts its lines or a claim that an orchard yields fruit in winter. Honest, independent graders miss traps in scattered, random ways. Sybils run by one operator share a model and prompt, so they miss the same traps the same way. That matching error pattern acts like a lantern on the cluster, whose keys then split one reward.
